title: PostHog vs Plausible
description: PostHog vs Plausible — compare product analytics with flags and replay vs simple privacy-first web analytics.
verdict: PostHog is a product analytics suite for SaaS teams that need events, funnels, retention, session replay, feature flags, and experiments. Plausible is a privacy-first web analytics tool for marketing sites that need clean traffic and goal reports without GA4 complexity.
quickAnswer: **PostHog** is the better fit if you need **in-product behavior, flags, and experiments**. **Plausible** is the better fit if you need **simple, privacy-respecting website analytics** with a lightweight script and optional self-hosting.
bottomLine: Do not treat these as peers unless you only need pageviews. For blogs and marketing sites, Plausible (or Fathom) wins on simplicity, privacy posture, and script weight. For product-led SaaS, PostHog wins on capability — at the cost of heavier instrumentation and a much larger script on our recorded benchmark.

faq.question: Can Plausible replace PostHog?
faq.answer: No for product teams. Plausible does not offer feature flags, experiments, session replay, or deep retention/cohort product analytics.

faq.question: Can PostHog replace Plausible?
faq.answer: For basic website traffic, yes — but it is usually overkill. If you only need referrers and pageviews, Plausible is simpler, lighter, and often cheaper to operate mentally even when PostHog’s free tier covers events.

faq.question: Which is better for a SaaS marketing site plus app?
faq.answer: Common pattern: Plausible (or similar) on the marketing site and PostHog in the product. Some teams run PostHog everywhere; weigh script weight and event taxonomy cost.

faq.question: Which is more privacy-friendly?
faq.answer: Plausible is designed as cookieless privacy-first web analytics. PostHog can be configured carefully (and self-hosted) but autocapture, identified users, and session replay increase privacy review surface.

faq.question: How do script sizes compare?
faq.answer: On our Slow-4G fixture, Plausible transferred about 3.2 KiB with ~+250 ms load overhead. PostHog transferred about 144 KiB with ~+1.29 s overhead. Full results are on the [benchmarks](/benchmarks/) pages.

editorialNotes.title: Category mismatch is the point
editorialNotes.content: Founders often search this pair when deciding whether a "simple analytics" tool is enough. If your questions are product questions, Plausible will feel empty quickly. If your questions are traffic questions, PostHog will feel heavy and noisy.

editorialNotes.title: Self-hosting
editorialNotes.content: Both offer self-hosted paths. Plausible’s self-hosted edition is a lighter ops footprint than full PostHog (ClickHouse/Kafka class). Most startups should start on each vendor’s cloud and revisit self-hosting for compliance or cost later.
